analogyReview.scope: Fresh reread of all 32 active lessons: 15 analogy callouts (13 added, 2 converted from prose) checked for mapping and stated limits against the cited primary sources, with required facts outside the disclosure; 17 lessons recorded as not needing one, each with a reason.

lin-array-index-address.rationale: Equal-width plots map base/size/index; the limits (byte addresses, computed not travelled, uniform width) are correct.

lin-array-cache-row-layout.rationale: Reading a page across vs down maps row-major lines and a cache-line 'glance'; the limit names finite capacity, eviction, prefetching and loop interchange.

lin-array-operations-capacity.rationale: The shift code and capacity diagram already give a concrete model; an analogy would repeat them.

lin-array-geometric-growth.rationale: dsa/01's amortised-append lesson already carries an analogy for the same mechanism; the series explanation here is direct.

lin-array-runtime-layouts.rationale: Address book vs terrace maps reference slots vs inline values; the limits (shared referents, headers, allocator overhead) are accurate.

lin-array-shrink-boundaries.rationale: Thermostat dead band maps separated grow/shrink thresholds; the limit notes that resize cost grows with the array and thresholds are exact counts.

lin-string-immutable-sharing.rationale: Printed editions and bookmarks map objects and references; the limits cover interning and CPython's unobservable in-place extension.

lin-string-unicode-units.rationale: Byte and code-unit tables with real strings are more precise than any analogy for the encoding layers.

lin-string-building-cost.rationale: Recopying a manuscript maps full-copy concatenation vs collect-then-join; the limits cover the in-place optimisation and copy speed.

lin-string-operation-pitfalls.rationale: A list of unrelated pitfalls; no single mechanism benefits from an analogy.

lin-list-node-traversal.rationale: Treasure-hunt clues map next pointers, traversal cost and insert-after; the limit covers the end marker, cache misses and non-consuming reads.

lin-list-rewire-singly.rationale: A short pointer procedure with a before/after diagram; the previous unit's analogy already covers links.

lin-list-doubly-sentinel.rationale: The ring and sentinel diagrams with runnable code are the clearest model.

lin-list-circular-tradeoffs.rationale: A survey of trade-offs grounded in real systems; no single mechanism to illustrate.

lin-list-reversal-pattern.rationale: A procedure with a full execution trace.

lin-list-middle-cycle-detection.rationale: Runners on a looped track map slow/fast and the identity meeting; the limit correctly says pointers move in whole nodes, so fast cannot jump over slow.

lin-list-cycle-entry-proof.rationale: The proof is the content, and the previous unit's track analogy covers the setting.

lin-list-dummy-gap-deletion.rationale: A boundary-case procedure with explicit traces.

lin-list-stable-merging.rationale: The merge trace is clearer than a card-dealing comparison.

lin-list-combining-patterns.rationale: Combines earlier patterns, each already explained.

lin-stack-storage-choices.rationale: Plate pile maps push/pop/peek and LIFO; the limits (no middle access by interface, array growth) are correct.

lin-stack-nested-state.rationale: The frame diagram and bracket traces are concrete.

lin-stack-postfix-evaluation.rationale: A procedure with a trace table.

lin-stack-shunting-yard.rationale: Railway siding maps the operator stack and output train; naming checked against the source. The limits note that precedence and brackets have no railway counterpart.

lin-stack-monotonic-work.rationale: The waiting-index explanation is concrete; the monotonic-deque lesson carries the dominated-candidate analogy.

lin-queue-fifo-shifting.rationale: Shop line maps enqueue/dequeue and pop(0) shifting with a 'now serving' marker; the limits cover leaving from the middle and serial element moves.

lin-queue-ring-indices.rationale: Clock face maps slots and wrap-round; reworded so the mapping does not depend on the hidden card. The limits cover empty/full and 1–12 vs 0-based numbering.

lin-queue-ring-full-overload.rationale: Waiting area maps the bounded buffer and backpressure; the limit says bounding does not raise throughput.

lin-queue-deque-ends.rationale: Executable maxlen and end-operation examples are the mechanism; the shop-line analogy is two units earlier.

lin-queue-bfs-distances.rationale: Ripples map BFS distance rings; the limits cover discrete processing along edges and equal edge lengths.

lin-queue-monotonic-windows.rationale: Shortlist maps back pops of dominated items and front expiry; the limits cover single-number comparison, positions vs time and ties.

lin-queue-priority-ties.rationale: The emergency-department and scheduler examples are real uses; tie-breaking is shown by executable code.
